<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s).

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via file_abc (literal, a string literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via TursoDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via no_sql_seam (literal, a string literal in skipped), os migrate files-to-references (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/files-to-references.ts))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via TursoDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via os migrate files-to-references (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/files-to-references.ts))_
- `content/docs/upgrading.mdx`  _(via os migrate files-to-references (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/files-to-references.ts))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via os migrate files-to-references (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/files-to-references.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fc6ddb87a4cd065171080f018cd865cd9c84c9d9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f635112db4fb1c2dbc4ddd0e920cd37f8da9d561` — the merge of head `672da75c7c2c5f990a306e6866de2c654e4385dd` into base `fc6ddb87a4cd065171080f018cd865cd9c84c9d9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f635112db4fb1c2dbc4ddd0e920cd37f8da9d561 && git checkout f635112db4fb1c2dbc4ddd0e920cd37f8da9d561
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fc6ddb87a4cd065171080f018cd865cd9c84c9d9 672da75c7c2c5f990a306e6866de2c654e4385dd && git checkout -B drift-repro fc6ddb87a4cd065171080f018cd865cd9c84c9d9 && git merge --no-ff 672da75c7c2c5f990a306e6866de2c654e4385dd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fc6ddb87a4cd065171080f018cd865cd9c84c9d9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fc6ddb87a4cd065171080f018cd865cd9c84c9d9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `672da75c7c2c5f990a306e6866de2c654e4385dd`

Scope read:
- the diff `61609edf8..672da75c7` (5 files);
- card #19894 and its comments (the os-dev report is treated as a claim), including the claim amendment 5820204593;
- the PR body;
- AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist step 3, Prime Directives) and `contract-review.md`;
- the on-main precedent `.changeset/17080-per-release-spec-changes.md`;
- the check runs at head via REST, polled until nothing was in progress.

Probes ran in the reviewer's own worktree at head, which was removed afterwards; no derived gate family was re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The remote refusal of `planMediaColumnMove()` is reachable only in remote mode: RIGHT.**
   - The override is `if (this.isRemote) refuseRemoteMediaColumnMove(); return super.planMediaColumnMove();`. `detectMode` answers `remote` only for a remote-scheme url with no `syncUrl`.
   - The non-remote arm is the inherited path, byte for byte.
   - Measured:
     - the driver pin runs 9/9 green;
     - local `:memory:` and `file:` scans equal a plain `SqlDriver` scan of the same declaration, and replica plans 2 `unquote` moves;
     - with the guard line removed, the 3 remote cases go red with `expected a refusal, got an answer: {"dialect":"sqlite","plans":[],"refusals":[]}`, and the 6 controls stay green.
   - Mechanism, confirmed in driver-sql: `managedObjectFields` is filled only via `registerManagedObjectMetadata`, which only `SqlDriver.initObjects` reaches. The three remote doors (`syncSchema`, `initObjects`, `syncSchemasBatch`) register through `registerExternalObject`, which fills `mediaFields` only.
   - Probe per door: `doc` and `pic` are TEXT on the remote double, `managedObjectFields` is empty, `mediaFields` is `{m:[doc,pic]}`, and the placeholder Knex's `hasTable('m')` is false.
   - Other callers: `git grep planMediaColumnMove` finds one runtime caller, the CLI command. No other in-repo behaviour changes.
2. **The command change: RIGHT.** Only `error?.code === NOT_IMPLEMENTED` becomes `skipped: 'driver_cannot_plan'`. Measured through `MigrateFilesToReferences.run`:
   - **`--apply --yes --json` with a refusing planner:** exit 0. The document carries `gatePassed: true`, `flag.passed: true`, `backfill`, `verify`, `columnMove: null`, `columnsMovedAt: null` and `columnMoveRefused: {error, code: "NOT_IMPLEMENTED"}`. The dry run has the same shape with `flag: null`.
   - **Text face:** exit 0. Both reports print, then the flag line, then exactly one `Column step: NOT JUDGED …` line, and no "nothing to move".
   - **Any other throw:** `ECONNRESET` and a codeless `Error` still give exit 1 and the outer-catch envelope.
   - **Exit code:** the self-check's. With the gate not passed and a refusing planner, the command exits 1, calls the planner 0 times, and `columnMoveRefused` is null.
   - **`columnMoveRefused`:** present, and `null`, on every full-report path (gate not passed, no SQL driver, empty scan, dry run). It is absent from the early-exit error envelopes, which never carried `columnMove` either.
   - **The flag:** recorded before the column step, so it stays recorded on a refusal, and `columns_moved_at` is never stamped. The prose matches.
   - **Status:** `errorCodeFields` forwards `httpStatus` and drops `status`, so the key is `{error, code}` with no 501. That is consistent with the changeset's `{ error, code }`.
3. **The static import of `StandardErrorCode` from `@objectstack/spec/api` breaks no rule.**
   - #5726's pin matches only `@objectstack/driver-*` specifiers.
   - eslint restricts only root-namespace `@objectstack/spec` imports, and `/api` is a published subpath (`exports` entry, dist present).
   - `@objectstack/spec` is a `dependencies` entry of `@objectstack/cli`, and 18 other command modules already value-import `@objectstack/spec` subpaths.
   - Lint & Repo Gates and every Type Check lane are green.
4. **The pins fail without the fix: RIGHT, reproduced.**
   - Driver: guard removed gives 3 red and 6 green.
   - CLI: with `files-to-references.ts` at the merge base, 4 red and 1 green. The three refusal pins fail on the exit code, the empty-scan control fails on the missing key, and the `ECONNRESET` control stays green.
   - Base behaviour re-measured: `--apply --yes --json` with a refusing planner printed exactly `{"error":…,"code":"NOT_IMPLEMENTED"}` and exited 1.
5. **CI at this head:** 34 runs, 0 in progress, 0 failures, 31 success, and 3 skipped (Console Pin Gate, Build Docs, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)). Every required context is `success`: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core (6/6), Dogfood Regression Gate (3/3), Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL) and Governed Surface Queue Guard. Check Changeset is green.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`: RIGHT.**
  - The widening: the `os migrate files-to-references --json` document gains `columnMoveRefused`. The precedent `.changeset/17080-per-release-spec-changes.md` declares a new `os validate --json` key as `Clause-②: yes (widening)`.
  - The narrowing: remote `TursoDriver.planMediaColumnMove()` now throws where it resolved `{plans:[],refusals:[]}`.
  - `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` names `yes (narrowing)` as exactly this combination. Option B (`no (narrowing)`) would deny the widening against the repo's own precedent, so amendment 5820204593's choice of A is correct.
- Both packages are `minor` (`@objectstack/driver-turso`, `@objectstack/cli`). There is no `major`, and no `patch` on a package whose `src/**` moves.
- The ADR-0087 marker is present, well-formed and true: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Nothing authorable is removed, renamed or reshaped, `planMediaColumnMove` keeps its name and declared return type, and the body carries no FROM → TO prescription.
- The BREAKING banner is right, and correctly scoped to callers that plan the move on a remote Turso datasource.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Changeset, sentence by sentence:** every sentence is **TRUE**.
- The title, and the `Clause-②` line.
- The banner: the remote face throws `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` / `501` where it answered an empty scan (pinned on all three doors), and local and replica plan exactly as before, the local modes exactly as `SqlDriver` does (measured).
- The three-door measurement: each door holds the two TEXT media columns (`pragma table_info` per door) and answered an empty scan on every door (ablation).
- The mechanism: the planner walks objects no remote door registers, and probes through the placeholder in-memory Knex.
- The local and replica faces plan two `unquote` moves.
- The command printed "nothing to move" for the empty scan (measured on base, verbatim).
- Bullet 1:
  - the planner runs after the backfill and self-check, and after the flag is recorded;
  - the pre-change error-only envelope with exit 1, re-measured on base;
  - `NOT JUDGED` on the text face, and `columnMoveRefused` `{ error, code }` or `null` beside `columnMove: null` / `columnsMovedAt: null`, true for the report document;
  - the reports are emitted, nothing is stamped, and the exit code is the self-check's.
- Bullet 2: any other throw still fails the command (`ECONNRESET` and a codeless error measured).
- Bullet 3: an empty scan still reads "nothing to move".
- Bullet 4: no new error code. `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` is a `StandardErrorCode` member, and the four sibling builders set the same code and status.
- "If you are refused": the backfill, self-check and flag are unaffected, and the remote face writes `"file_abc"` and reads `file_abc`. The resolver it is given is asked 0 times, and by code `resolveFileColumnsMoved` is reached only from `SqlDriver.initObjects`.
- The ADR-0087 marker text.

**The refusal message (`refuseRemoteMediaColumnMove`), sentence by sentence:** all 5 sentences are TRUE.
1. Unsupported on the REMOTE transport, thrown only under `isRemote`.
2. The planner reads through the placeholder Knex and walks objects that remote mode registers another way (measured).
3. "Nothing to move" would be the answer for every remote database. Nothing was planned and nothing ran: 0 statements (pinned).
4. It is a capability gap, so NOT_IMPLEMENTED/501 and not a 400, with the same rationale as the siblings.
5. Remote mode keeps the JSON encoding and does not read the record of a completed move (pinned).

It carries no tracker id.

**The text-face warning line:** TRUE. "neither inspected nor moved" (0 statements), "no column move was recorded" (the stamp path is unreachable), "stays on the JSON encoding" (the driver's arm; same wording as the existing `no_sql_seam` line), and "The driver says: …".

**PR body:** every sentence judged TRUE. That covers the Clause-② section, "What changed", the H1–H5 tables and readings (re-measured), the verification counts, the unit-tier claim, and the four Acceptance notes. Out-of-band stamping is UNMEASURED, and the PR declares it so.

**The os-dev report's open question and flags:**
- Clause-② A or B: **A**, as answered above.
- The refusal names no remedy transport: **accepted**. A "local copy" remedy would be false here, because moving a local copy does not move the remote database.
- The README class-(a) finding (`driver-turso/README.md` lists `RemoteTransport: beginTransaction, commit, rollback`, and the remote arms refuse all three): **REAL**. It is outside this card's class, so it should be filed separately.
- The remote face never asks the ADR-0104 resolver: **REAL** by code and pin. It is a capability gap, not a defect in this diff. The filing decision is the seat's.
- `errorCodeFields` drops `status`: **REAL**, measured, pre-existing and repo-wide. The filing decision is the seat's.
- A non-refusal throw after an `--apply` backfill replaces the report: **REAL** by code, pre-existing, with no named reproduction. The note stands.
- The process notes (early vitest runs outside the lock, the commit trailers): no bearing on the shipped surface. The trailers are AGENTS.md's model-free pair.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-19894-turso-remote-media-column-move`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Bvd69VPa6puiNzzPUroDBx`

**VERDICT: PASS**

This record is both the at-tier clause-② review the declared `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` requires and the prose review of the changeset and the shipped messages.

Isolated reviewer: a contract-review-tier subagent, fed only the card, the PR, the claim amendment, the precedent changeset and AGENTS.md; adopted by the seat.
